name: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
label: Touch and Go
lede: Ted Leo named his band after a dub-soaked solo record, rode out money trouble at Lookout! and Touch and Go's shutdown, and took Shake the Sheets back on the road twenty years after it came out.

eras.title: From a Notre Dame band to a one-man pharmacy
eras.text: Before the Pharmacists there was Chisel, the trio Leo started in college and ran for seven years. When it ended, he made records for friends, sang in a band that didn't last, and then made a strange solo album that gave him a name for everything after.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chisel
years.h: Ted Leo starts Chisel at the University of Notre Dame
years.p: The New Jersey hardcore kid forms the trio with bassist Chris Infante and drummer John Dugan. Chris Norborg takes over bass in 1992, and the band makes two albums for Gern Blandsten.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chisel · Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Chisel plays its last show, in Knoxville
years.p: West Coast and European dates for Set You Free are cancelled. Wikipedia says the depression Leo was fighting on tour made it hard for him to want to go on.
years.xp: Leo spent the next stretch on other people's records, producing for [[The Spinanes|ea8aba9a-0163-439b-91ff-fe02e9d67663]], The Secret Stars and Jejune. He also fronted the Sin-Eaters, a short-lived band with members of [[The Van Pelt|4ce909db-0da6-4eed-bfe6-6c1f71e265b0]] and Native Nod, the band his brother Chris Leo had played in.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: A solo record full of dub and tape tricks names the band
years.p: Gern Blandsten puts out tej leo(?), Rx / pharmacists: Leo alone, mixing punk with reggae, dub and audio experiments. Wikipedia counts it as technically the first Pharmacists album.
years.xp: The same year, Persona Records issued the Guitar for Jodi 7-inch, with a demo of The Great Communicator, and Garbage Czar put out a split single with One AM Radio on which Leo covers [[Lungfish|5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e]]'s To Whom You Were Born.

eras.title: The Pharmacists get a band, then a label
eras.text: Leo built a real group around the solo project, lost half of it within a year, and signed to Lookout!, the East Bay pop-punk label that was trying out a wider sound. The first full-band album came together with whoever was in the room.

years.src: Wikipedia: James Canty · Wikipedia: Ted Leo
years.h: Nation of Ulysses' drummer joins Leo on guitar
years.p: [[James Canty|ffc732f4-15a3-42e1-a498-965c1d793e35]] plays guitar, Jodi Buonanno bass and [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]] drums on the Treble in Trouble EP for Ace Fu, the first release by a full Pharmacists band.
years.xp: Canty had drummed in [[Nation of Ulysses|ae888df0-2a19-4895-a654-e0093875d5b6]] and played guitar and keys in [[The Make-Up|26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a]]; he's the younger brother of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] drummer [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]]. Leo met Buonanno in the late '90s, when both were touring in bands, and later married her.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Lookout! signs the band as the rhythm section leaves
years.p: Buonanno and Farina step out, and Leo and Canty go into the studio with a rotating set of bassists and drummers.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Tyranny of Distance · Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Brendan Canty produces The Tyranny of Distance
years.p: Five people take turns on drums, Brendan Canty and Leo's brother Danny among them. Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and later ranked it No. 120 of the decade.
years.xp:
The title comes from a line in Split Enz's Six Months in a Leaky Boat, which Leo went on to cover twice: solo in 2003 and with the full band in 2005. Pete Kerlin and Alex Minoff split the bass parts; Seb Thompson, the Cantys and both Leos drum.

AllMusic's Nate Cavalieri heard punk and retro pop fused with a noisy love of '60s blues-rock. Pitchfork's Chip Chanko singled out "a uniquely expressive voice, and a perfect single."

years.cap: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists at WHCL's "Rock Your Indie Heart" festival
years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists · Wikipedia: Hearts of Oak
years.h: The tour band becomes the band
years.p: Bassist Dave Lerner, drummer Chris Wilson and keyboardist Dorien Garry join for good during the Tyranny tours, and the five cut the next album that September.

eras.title: Rude boys on network TV
eras.text: Three records on Lookout! made the Pharmacists one of the best-reviewed bands in indie rock. Hearts of Oak got the year-end lists, a festival set became a film, and by Shake the Sheets the band was down to three.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hearts of Oak · Wikipedia: Ted Leo
years.h: Hearts of Oak scores an 84 on Metacritic
years.p: Leo and Nicolas Vernhes produce. Spin put it at No. 14 of 2003, and Pitchfork later ranked it No. 59 of the 2000s.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.3, Spin 9 out of 10, Alternative Press five stars. Critics heard everything from Thin Lizzy to Elvis Costello. Jodi Buonanno is credited with clapping, whistling and backing vocals.
play: Where Have All the Rude Boys Gone?

yt: Where Have All the Rude Boys Gone?, live on Conan, 2003
years.h: Where Have All the Rude Boys Gone? goes out on Conan
years.p: The band plays the Hearts of Oak single on Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

years.cap: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists at Cornell University, Ithaca, November 2003
years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
yt: Dirty Old Town, the Siren Festival film
years.h: A Coney Island festival set turns into a movie
years.p: The band's show at the 2003 Siren Music Festival becomes Dirty Old Town, a documentary Plexifilm releases on DVD in early 2004.

years.cap: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists live, December 2004
years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Garry and Canty leave, and the Pharmacists are a trio
years.p: Leo, Lerner and Wilson make the next album as a three-piece.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shake the Sheets · Wikipedia: The Tyranny of Distance · Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Chris Shaw records Shake the Sheets at Avatar
years.p: Cut in New York in under three weeks in May and June 2004, the last Lookout! album is the band's most political. Blender called it "a pop-punk update on Springsteen."
years.xp:
Sessions ran May 17 to 19 at Avatar Studios and May 20 to June 5 at Stratosphere. Metacritic has it at 79. Wikipedia says the single Me and Mia is about a friend of Leo's who had an eating disorder.

In 2005 the band followed it with the iTunes-only Sharkbite Sessions EP, including the full-band take on Six Months in a Leaky Boat.

eras.title: Touch and Go, a pool party and the convention
eras.text: A move to Chicago's Touch and Go put the band on a label with real distribution just as the festivals came calling. The line-up shifted again, and the band answered the 2008 Republican National Convention with a benefit EP.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists · Wikipedia: Lookout! Records
years.h: Out of a struggling Lookout!, into Touch and Go
years.p: The band leaves Lookout! amid the label's financial crises, as Wikipedia puts it, and signs with Touch and Go in Chicago.
years.xp: Lookout!'s trouble started in 2005, when several high-profile artists took back the rights to their Lookout! records, a loss that hit the label's royalty payments for years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Coachella, then Pitchfork Music Festival
years.p: Constant touring and big festival bills grow the band's audience in the year before the Touch and Go debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Living with the Living · Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
yt: Timorous Me, live in San Francisco, March 2007
years.h: Back with Brendan Canty for the Touch and Go debut
years.p: Recorded at Longview Farms in Massachusetts and Canty's Blind Spot Studios in D.C., Living with the Living enters the Billboard 200 at No. 109 on about 8,000 first-week copies.
years.xp:
First pressings came with the Mo' Living EP, and iTunes buyers got The Vain Parade. Reviews were mixed: Pitchfork gave it 7.5, and Rolling Stone's Christian Hoard liked the spry rhythms but found it short on memorable songs.

James Canty came back to play guitar on the tours that followed.

years.src: Punknews: Ted Leo And The Pharmacists part ways
years.h: Leo toasts Dave Lerner with bubbly at McCarren Park Pool
years.p: The Brooklyn pool show is Lerner's last after five years on bass. Punknews, citing Pitchfork, called the split amicable.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists · Wikimedia Commons: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: The Pharmacists play Bumbershoot in Seattle
years.p: A Labor Day weekend set at the Seattle festival, three weeks after Lerner's farewell at the pool.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Marty "Violence" Key of the Young Pioneers takes over bass
years.p: Key, formerly of the Young Pioneers, fills in on the fall tour and stays.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Pearl Jam takes the band out for six dates
years.p: After opening six U.S. shows for [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]], the Pharmacists tour with [[Against Me!|a66ebddc-ff04-46b8-820a-15c63e80dba1]] and Future of the Left that fall.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Rapid Response answers the St. Paul convention violence
years.p: A surprise digital EP sold through Touch and Go's site at a price of the buyer's choosing, with all proceeds going to Democracy Now! and Food Not Bombs St. Paul.

eras.title: Matador, and a trio again
eras.text: Touch and Go stopped distributing records, and the Pharmacists' sixth album came out on Matador. It's the last full-length the band has made.

years.src: Wikipedia: Touch and Go Records · Wikipedia: The Brutalist Bricks
years.h: Touch and Go stops making and distributing records
years.p: Corey Rusk announces the downsizing, citing the economy. The next Pharmacists album comes out on Matador.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Brutalist Bricks · Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: The Brutalist Bricks lands on Matador
years.p: Made at Seaside Lounge in Brooklyn and Radium City in Wakefield, Rhode Island. Pitchfork called it the best record from "one of the greats in six rocky years."
years.xp: It reached No. 114 on the Billboard 200 and No. 11 on the independent chart, and Exclaim! named it the third-best punk album of 2010. Spin's reviewer welcomed its "Dischordant burn." A Record Store Day 7-inch, The Oldest House, came out the same spring.

years.cap: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists at Neumos, Seattle
years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Marty Key quits to open a record store
years.p: The band carries on as a trio, with James Canty moving to bass.

eras.title: Debt, a Kickstarter and the long way back
eras.text: Leo spent the 2010s on a duo with Aimee Mann, a crowdfunded solo album and paying off a bad tour. The Pharmacists kept coming back for shows and anniversary runs, and new songs went straight to Bandcamp.

years.cap: Aimee Mann and Ted Leo at the Pabst Theater, Milwaukee
years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo · Exclaim!
years.h: Leo and Aimee Mann become the Both
years.p: After months opening for Aimee Mann, Leo starts writing with her. Their album comes out in 2014 on Mann's own SuperEgo label.
years.xp: Exclaim! reports that a contract dispute with Matador over the Both record ended with Mann releasing it herself. Leo says he left Matador amicably, though the parting wasn't easy.

q: It was depressing until I started to see it as fertile, incubating time.
years.src: Exclaim! · Wikipedia: Ted Leo · Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: The Hanged Man arrives, paid for on Kickstarter
years.p: Leo crowdfunded his first album under his own name, Exclaim! reported, after a disastrous European tour left him in debt. Canty, Key and Wilson tour it with him.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the record grew out of years of career and personal hardship, including the loss of a daughter to a late-term miscarriage in 2011. Leo told Exclaim! he hoped the touring would help him crawl out of debt.

Members of the Pharmacists play on it, and saxophonist Adrian Berry joined the live band for the 2017–19 tours, which also marked 15 years of Hearts of Oak.

years.h: The Pharmacists turn up on KEXP in Seattle
years.p: A full session for the Seattle station, filmed during the run of tours behind The Hanged Man.

years.src: Punknews: Ted Leo and The Pharmacists announce riverboat gig
years.h: A gig on the Liberty Belle riverboat
years.p: The band and Frankie Rose play a cruise that docks on Manhattan's east side.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: New songs go straight to Bandcamp, plus a Stereolab cover
years.p: Andy, Come Out has two new songs and Stereolab's Ping Pong, played live the night before. The Old 200 follows a month later, all credited to the Pharmacists.

yt: Full set at the Black Cat, Washington, D.C.
years.h: A full set at the Black Cat, back in Washington
years.p: A fan films the whole show at the D.C. club, near where the band started.

years.cap: Shake the Sheets anniversary tour, the Great Hall, Toronto
years.src: Wikipedia: Shake the Sheets · Wikipedia: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
years.h: Twenty years on, Shake the Sheets goes back on the road
years.p: Announced in February, the anniversary tour runs from June into November with Ekko Astral and Diners opening.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ted Leo
years.h: Gang of Four hire Leo for their farewell tour
years.p: He's announced as guitarist for the band's Long Goodbye tour.
